## Pre-registered hypotheses (protocol section 6)

| Test | pairs | mean relative difference | 95% CI | wins | Wilcoxon p | Holm p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 Mamba vs w/o selectivity (Amazon) | 15 | +2.33% | [-0.09%, +4.58%] | 11/15 | 0.23 | 0.69 |
| H2 Last+mean vs Mamba (Amazon) | 15 | +0.67% | [-0.62%, +1.92%] | 9/15 | 0.45 | 0.88 |
| H4a Mamba vs Last+mean (ML-1M) | 5 | +26.96% | [+25.28%, +28.42%] | 5/5 | 0.062 | 0.31 |
| H4b SASRec vs Last+mean (ML-1M) | 5 | +12.78% | [+12.23%, +13.32%] | 5/5 | 0.062 | 0.31 |
| H5 Mamba vs w/o selectivity (ML-1M) | 5 | +0.92% | [-0.75%, +2.51%] | 3/5 | 0.44 | 0.88 |

Mamba's NDCG@10 drop when the most recent item is removed: baby 30.8%, sports 33.7%, clothing 33.0%

Verdicts:

- H1 selectivity gain small on Amazon (CI upper < 3%): **does not hold**
- H2 last+mean non-inferior to Mamba on Amazon (CI lower > -3%): **holds**
- H3 Mamba loses >= 20% without the last item on every Amazon dataset: **holds**
- H4 on ML-1M Mamba and SASRec beat last+mean by >= 5% (CI lower > 0): **holds**
- H5 on ML-1M selectivity helps (CI lower > 0): **does not hold**
